findings.summary: The write-rights test only checks that a word is present, so a negated or vague phrase counts.
findings.evidence: ENV_WRITE_RIGHTS_WORDS only requires one of write/writes/written/writable/readonly/permission(s) somewhere in the assumption, so 'saved by main, restored by pull requests, never written' meets the write part. The doc comment admits a nearby gap (a pasted CI block with write and scope words can meet those parts without saying who writes shared entries) but not this exact case. It matches the existing check's word-list style; a stricter version would require a write word next to a ref or scope word.

findings.summary: The reader's own instructions don't mention cache scope yet, so the reader learns the rule only from the refusal error.
findings.evidence: CHANGELOG names 'Follow-up, not done here: add the cache clause to the reader rule line in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs'. That file is outside the deliverables, and naming it as follow-up fits the root-cause default.

summary: Pass. The change extends `check_environment_reach` in surveys.rs, the reading-stage check where the missing step originates. It now fires in three cases: a behavior criterion that ties a CI place to a cache or artifact word (or names `actions/cache` or the upload/download artifact actions); a CI result reused across refs, with SHA-matched results excluded; and a created or modified `.github/workflows/` deliverable that mentions a cache. When it fires, the reading needs one `Environment:` assumption that names the cache and states save scope, restore scope, write rights and ref scope, and the error names only the missing parts. The doc comment and CHANGELOG name the cause, the two jobs, the two introspections and the 3% estimate. I ran the 5 new unit tests, the refusal corpus (23/23, including the new declaration test) and the edited defined-terms test; all pass on this snapshot. Athena's revert runs show the new tests fail without the fix (exit 101). fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in the recorded CI run. The replay newly refused 0 of 50 recent accepted readings, against the declared 3% estimate. All four changed files are on the deliverables list. Two minor findings: (1) the write-rights test only checks that a word such as "write" or "written" is present, so "never written" would pass; the doc comment notes a nearby gap but not this one; (2) the reader prompt line in briefs.rs is not updated yet; the CHANGELOG names it as follow-up work.
